transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-12 14:00 PST | Duration: 65 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SRE), Priya Raman (Atlas Head of ML), Mark Ellison (Atlas Platform Eng), Sarah Torres (Atlas SecOps), Evan Kline (Atlas Dev Lead)
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — everyone can hear me?
[00:10] Priya: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Samir.
[00:15] Samir: Cool. The goal today is a hands-on technical deep dive around observability — OpenTelemetry, token-level metrics, traces for KV cache, batching, quantization, and how that all works in a VPC/on-prem flow. Lena will drive most of the demos.
[00:30] Lena: Hi all — I'll kick off with a quick architecture sketch, then show an example trace and the metrics we emit. Also we have an example OTEL collector config and Grafana dashboards. Note some of the names in the trace are internal shorthand, so we'll share a mapping.
[01:00] Mark: Quick ask — we run Datadog + Prometheus today, want to make sure we can correlate Redwood traces to our request ids and our Datadog spans.
[01:10] Lena: Absolutely. We emit OTLP over gRPC to your collector or our private collector if you're on Redwood Private. You can add a span attribute request.id (we can map our request-id header to request.id). We'll show that in the config.
[01:30] Diego: Important to call out — in Dedicated and Private, the control plane can push logs to your S3/bucket or to your SIEM via forwarding. For token-level telemetry we only emit aggregate counters unless you opt-in to richer traces; we avoid logging PII or full prompt text by default.
[02:00] Sarah: That was one of our main concerns — data residency and secrets. Do you support KMS/HSM for trace encryption on Private?
[02:08] Lena: Yes, Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and the OTEL exporter can be configured to use TLS mutual auth inside the VPC. We'll include the config snippet.
[02:30] [02:30] Samir: Let's jump into the trace example Lena mentioned.
[02:40] Lena: (shares screen) Here's a typical OpenTelemetry flame/span view for a single request. Top-level span is the HTTP request received by Redwood gateway, child spans include router decision, model dispatch, KV cache lookup, compilation/kernel selection, batch wait time, and token generation loop.
[03:10] Lena: Notice the KV cache span has attributes: cache.hit (true/false), cache.latency_ms, detected_prefix (hashed), and cache.size_est. We also add batching.batch_size and batching.wait_ms to the model worker spans.
[03:40] Evan: How do you correlate token-level timings? We need token-by-token latency breakdown for debugging hallucinations on long contexts.
[03:50] Lena: We emit token-level metrics as aggregate histograms (e.g., token.latency_ms bucketed, token.generated_count per request). Full per-token logs are opt-in and require agreement since prompts are sensitive. The histograms let you compute p50/p95/p99 token latency across prompts and correlate with KV cache hit rate.
[04:20] Priya: Can you show a sample metric name convention so our Grafana/Prometheus engineers can map them?
[04:28] Lena: Sure — examples: redwood.request.duration_ms, redwood.token.latency_ms_bucket, redwood.cache.hit_ratio, redwood.batching.batch_size_count, redwood.quantization.model_bits (labels: model, seq_len, hw_arch). We'll attach a full naming doc.
[04:55] Mark: We use OpenTelemetry -> Prometheus remote write. Any issues with label cardinality from token-level metrics?
[05:05] Lena: We recommend low-cardinality labels: model, region, env, deployment_id. Do NOT use full prompt hashes as labels. For prompt sets we suggest precomputing prompt_set_id and passing that as a label to keep cardinality bounded.
[05:30] [05:30] Diego: Also watch out for histogram explosion if you create too many label combinations (model x quantization x seq_len). We include a suggestion table in the docs.
[05:50] Sarah: Regarding KV cache, what metrics tell us when cache is degrading or causing tail latency?
[06:00] Lena: Cache hit ratio over time, cache.latency_ms histogram, cache.eviction_rate, and kv.prefetch_miss_count. High eviction_rate + lower hit ratio correlates with higher token generation latency p95.
[06:30] Priya: About batching: if you batch aggressively to save cost we worry about added latency. How do you show batching impact?
[06:40] Lena: batching.wait_ms and batching.batch_size are spans/attributes. You can compute the added queueing latency by looking at the batch wait span duration. We also emit redwood.batch.queue_time_ms as a metric. You can tag by SLO severity to detect when cost optimizations hit latency targets.
[07:00] Evan: For quantization, do you emit model-level quality metrics? Like per-version perplexity/regression alerts?
[07:10] Lena: We integrate model quality monitoring into Redwood Optimize. For telemetry we emit redwood.model.version and redwood.eval.regression_count for failed prompts in an eval set. Quantization is tagged as model.quantized=true and model.bits=8/4 etc.
[07:35] Priya: Can we get token-level quality traces for a small sample to debug hallucinations?
[07:43] Samir: We can enable a privacy-safe trace mode for a small set of requests — scrub PII, mask prompt text, and provide token-level timing and attention scores. That would be opt-in and limited to debug windows.
[08:05] Mark: For VPC / on-prem, how does tracing look different? We want to keep everything internal and not send data to Redwood hosted collectors.
[08:15] Lena: In VPC/on-prem, OTLP is local — you run your collector and route to your logging/monitoring stack. The Redwood agent inside the VPC emits spans to localhost:4317. All traces and token metrics stay inside your network unless you configure otherwise.
[08:40] Sarah: Does the on-prem runtime support the same metric names and semantic as hosted? We want parity.
[08:45] Diego: Yes — we maintain parity for metric names and spans. The only difference is where exporters point. There are a couple of env vars for toggling sensitive telemetry defaults.
[09:05] [09:05] Lena: I'll show a sample Grafana dashboard (shares). Top row: request throughput, p50/p95/p99 request latency. Second row: token latency histograms, cache hit ratio, batch size distribution. Third row: model CPU/GPU utilization and quantization efficiency.
[09:40] Priya: Can the dashboards be templatized to import into our Grafana?
[09:45] Lena: Yes we provide Grafana JSON dashboards you can import; we'll drop them into the shared drive link in the notes.
[10:00] Mark: On the secret side — are there audit logs for who accessed traces? We need RBAC for trace access.
[10:10] Diego: For Private we integrate with your SSO/IdP and maintain audit logs with span access events. For Hosted we have RBAC around the console and APIs; we'll share the SOC2 + audit logging docs.
[10:30] Sarah: Good. Also need to ensure trace retention policies match our compliance needs.
[10:35] Lena: Retention is configurable in Private; in Hosted you can request extended retention as an add-on. We'll share exact retention windows and costs.
[10:50] Evan: A bit of follow-up on kernel selection and telemetry — can you expose which kernel path was selected per request (e.g., fused-attn-v2 vs legacy)?
[11:00] Lena: Yes, we add an attribute runtime.kernel_name and runtime.kernel_version. That helps correlate perf regressions after runtime upgrades. It's a low-cardinality label.
[11:20] Priya: Let's talk about a benchmark plan. We want to validate p95 latency < 200ms for 2k token contexts on our critical prompt set.
[11:30] Samir: Great. Proposed plan: Redwood will stand up a Dedicated staging cluster, we will run a benchmark week with your prompt sets, with OTEL tracing enabled and dashboards. We'll iterate on batching/quantization settings and provide a report with token-level histograms and recommended config.
[11:55] Mark: Timeline?
[12:00] Samir: If we get prompt sets and credentials this week, we can target w/c 2025-02-24 for the benchmark week. Lena will send configs by 02-15.
[12:15] Priya: Sounds good. One last question — do you have example alerts for regressions that we can copy?
[12:25] Lena: Yes — alert examples: 1) alert if token.latency_ms.p95 increases > 25% vs baseline, 2) alert if cache.hit_ratio drops below 70% for 10m, 3) alert if batching.batch_size > configured threshold for > 5m. We'll include alert JSON for Prometheus Alertmanager and Datadog monitors.
[12:50] [12:50] Samir: Ok let's summarize and confirm owners. Lena will send OTEL collector + Grafana JSON + mapping doc. Diego will prepare Dedicated staging. Priya will share prompt sets and SLOs. Samir will follow up on pricing, SLA language, and security docs.
[13:10] Priya: Thanks everyone, this was super helpful.
[13:15] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up with the links and calendar invite for the benchmark week.
[13:20] Meeting end

Notes and links referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/observability , https://redwood.ai/docs/opentelemetry-example-config , shared drive: https://redwood-files.example.com/atlas/observability-dashboards , SOC2 doc: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-2024.pdf

Transcript notes: occasional ASR errors ("kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash"), speaker attribution sometimes generic at the start. Sensitive data: none included in this transcript — prompts to be provided offline under NDA.
